title: Oxford Quantum Circuits Releases Erado: An Open-Source Qiskit Simulator for Erasure Noise and Post-Selection - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Oxford Quantum Circuits open-sourced erado, a Qiskit simulator for erasure noise and post-selection, backed by a paper showing dual-rail postselection can beat the noise floor at the kiloquop scale when erasure-check error rates stay below 3%.

insights.claim: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) released erado, an open-source Python library that simulates erasure noise, dual-rail qubit encodings, and post-selection strategies on arbitrary Qiskit circuits, integrated as a 16-qubit AerSimulator backend inside OQC's QCaaS SDK.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives algorithm developers a free tool to benchmark erasure-aware error mitigation before running on real hardware, potentially accelerating third-party adoption of OQC's erasure-detection approach.

insights.claim: The companion paper 'The limits of erasure-based postselection for quantum error mitigation' (Griffiths et al., arXiv:2606.31428) shows postselection can fully mitigate the erasure channel when erasure check error rates stay below 3.0%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The 3.0% erasure-check error threshold is a concrete engineering target hardware teams need to hit for postselection-based mitigation to be viable.
insights.locator: demonstrates that postselection can fully mitigate the erasure channel

insights.claim: A postselected dual-rail qubit system can surpass the fundamental noise floor at the kiloquop (1,000 quantum operations) scale in a regime where a comparable single-rail architecture fails, justifying dual-rail encoding for NISQ algorithms ahead of full quantum error correction.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete performance case for choosing dual-rail hardware architectures as a bridge strategy before fault-tolerant QEC is achievable.
insights.locator: a postselected dual-rail system can surpass the fundamental noise floor

insights.claim: Erasure-detection methodologies and dual-rail architectures are being actively pursued beyond OQC across the industry, including by D-Wave Systems (following its acquisition of Quantum Circuits Inc.) and by Q-CTRL.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multiple independent players converging on dual-rail/erasure detection signals this is becoming a mainstream near-term error-mitigation strategy worth tracking across vendors, not an OQC-only bet.
insights.locator: Beyond OQC, erasure-detection methodologies and dual-rail architectures

insights.claim: D-Wave Systems acquired Quantum Circuits Inc. and is now also pursuing erasure-detection and dual-rail qubit approaches.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: M&A data point: D-Wave, historically an annealing specialist, is diversifying into gate-model error-mitigation IP via acquisition, a strategic pivot worth monitoring.
insights.locator: including by D-Wave Systems (following its acquisition of Quantum Circuits Inc.)

insights.claim: Erado provides precise parameter controls over false-positive and false-negative erasure detector rates, letting researchers quantify the exact trade-off point where the shot-rejection overhead of post-selection remains computationally profitable versus standard noisy sampling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Provides a reusable cost-benefit framework for deciding when post-selection error mitigation is worth its overhead, applicable across hardware platforms, not just OQC's.
insights.locator: By providing precise parameter controls over false-positive
